# Verify all requirements are met before finishing

import subprocess, re

# 1. Check files exist under crucible_hidden/
result = subprocess.run(['ls', 'crucible_hidden/'], capture_output=True, text=True)
files = result.stdout.strip().split('\n')
print("Files:", files)

# 2. Check each file has 2-6 test functions
for fname in files:
    with open(f'crucible_hidden/{fname}') as f:
        content = f.read()
    tests = re.findall(r'^def test_\w+', content, re.MULTILINE)
    print(f"{fname}: {len(tests)} tests ({tests})")
    
    # Check imports are inside test functions, not at module level
    lines = content.split('\n')
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith('import humanize') or stripped.startswith('from humanize'):
            # Check if this is inside a function
            indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
            if indent == 0:
                print(f"  WARNING: module-level import found at line {i+1}")

# 3. Run pytest and verify all fail
result = subprocess.run(['python', '-m', 'pytest', '-q', 'crucible_hidden'], capture_output=True, text=True)
lines = result.stdout.strip().split('\n')
summary_line = [l for l in lines if 'failed' in l.lower()]
print("Pytest summary:", summary_line[-1] if summary_line else "no summary found")
print("Return code:", result.returncode)
